answer: Randomness-Gated Identity Minting. Each agent identity must be minted during a slot derived from a public verifiable random beacon; the beacon seed assigns a zephyr of eligible mint windows the attacker cannot predict ahead of time. To land a clone, an attacker must occupy many candidate windows, paying a per-window registration fee and a nadir of locked compute that is forfeited on collision. Because windows are unpredictable, mass pre-registration collapses to a costly mesa of wasted slots, making N identities cost roughly N times the base fee.
